sources.field_scope: Commercial-license landing. It points to a mail application for commercial hunting, fishing, and trapping products. Trapping licenses and the quail game-holding permit can also be bought in a Go Outdoors Georgia account. The page does not list a fishing-guide product or a Toccoa roster.

sources.field_scope: Two-page commercial application, revision date 06-04-23, PDF created June 5, 2023. Licenses run April 1 through March 31. Products include commercial trapping, fish dealers, a catch-out pond, taxidermy, fur dealers, and commercial fishing defined as fishing for sale or with commercial gear. The form has no guide, charter, trout, or outfitter checkbox. The mail street was not copied.

sources.publisher: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division
sources.field_scope: Announcement dated October 20, 2026. Delayed harvest begins November 1, 2026. From November 1 to May 14 the five named streams are catch-and-release and limited to single-hook artificial lures. The Toccoa reach is Forest Service land upstream of Lake Blue Ridge in Fannin County, from 0.4 miles above Shallowford Bridge to 450 feet above the Sandy Bottom Canoe Access. The tailwater downstream of the dam is listed as a separate year-round trout water, not as delayed harvest. Anglers need a Georgia fishing license and a trout license. Not a guide roster.
sources.attribution: Cite the October 20, 2026 Wildlife Resources Division announcement.

sources.publisher: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division
sources.field_scope: Trout page. Anglers age 16 or older need a fishing license and a trout license. The Toccoa is named twice: as a delayed-harvest stream, and, downstream of Lake Blue Ridge Dam, as stocked rainbow and brown trout water. The page does not give a guide list, a boat field, or a printed revision date. It warns that many trout streams are on private property.
sources.attribution: Cite the Wildlife Resources Division trout page and the access date.

sources.publisher: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division
sources.field_scope: 2026 trout stocking list. PDF created May 7, 2026. Stocking runs March through October. Three Toccoa-area rows were read. Blue Ridge Tailwaters, Fannin County, is on the weekly table. Toccoa River, Fannin County, is on that table with the note that it is stocked weekly until July 4 and twice monthly afterward. Lake Blue Ridge, Fannin County, is on the once-each-year table. No guide, boat, or access-ramp column. The rest of the statewide water list was not counted.
sources.bulk: A water-and-county stocking list. Not a guide file.
sources.attribution: Cite the 2026 trout stocking list, created May 7, 2026.

sources.publisher: U.S. Forest Service, Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest
sources.field_scope: Open-season handout for outfitting and guiding, recreation events, and research. PDF created July 20, 2023 and modified July 24, 2023. Open seasons are February 1-28 for use from July 1 through December 31, and August 1-31 for use from January 1 through June 30. A temporary permit is capped at 200 service days in 180 days, and only one permit is issued per holder per use area in that period. Service days count each client. The forest asks holders to operate on temporary permits for two or three years before a priority permit of up to 10 years. The holder must indemnify the United States and name the United States as an additional insured. No dollar minimum was recovered from the text layer. The packet has no Toccoa field and no public holder list. A guide roster in the packet is a list the applicant must send, not a list the forest publishes. The permits mailbox was not copied.
sources.bulk: An application packet. Not an issued-permit file.
sources.attribution: Cite the Chattahoochee-Oconee open-season handout, file date July 24, 2023.
sources.request_process: Submit an open-season application to the forest permits mailbox printed in the packet, or ask the ranger district. No one was contacted.

sources.field_scope: Bookable Toccoa River float trips in Blue Ridge, plus private and public wade trips. Each boat seats two anglers plus a guide. The page says multiple boats are available, up to eight people. No boat name, length, builder, or documentation number. Anglers 16 and older need a Georgia fishing license. The page does not mention a trout license or a guide credential. No copyright line was on the homepage. The linked terms page does not grant directory reuse.
sources.bulk: A capacity statement. Not a count of identified hulls.
sources.request_process: None published for directory use. No one was contacted.

sources.field_scope: Guided float, public wade, and private trophy trips. Float trips are for one or two anglers per boat and are described on the Toccoa. No length, name, or documentation number. Guests buy their own fishing license for the state of the trip. The shop says it operates in Georgia, Tennessee, and North Carolina, so a float is not assumed to be the Toccoa unless the page says so. Footer copyright 2026, all rights reserved. The street was not copied.
sources.bulk: One boat-capacity claim. Not an identified hull.
